340049.title: Conjecture on list chromatic number of triangle-free graphs
340049.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, and let $\chi_\ell(G)$ denote its list chromatic number. **List-colouring conjecture.** There are constants $C_1,C_2>0$ such that

$$
\chi_\ell(G)\leq C_1\sqrt{n/\log n}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\chi_\ell(G)\leq C_2m^{1/3}/(\log m)^{2/3}.
$$

The paper describes these natural list-colouring versions as open problems, extending the fractional colouring questions to list chromatic number.

source.note: All triangle-free graphs, simultaneous n and m list-colouring bounds. Fractional colourings do not lift to arbitrary lists; no full uniform probabilistic construction. Small log-domain endpoints are wording issues, zero discovery credit. Primary unread.

340077.title: Convergence of cascade tree decomposition KL divergence to zero
340077.literal_statement: Let $\underline{X}$ be the input random vector and let $\underline{X}_{{\mathcal M}_i}$ denote the model random vector obtained after $i$ cascade-tree stages. The preceding theorem establishes only that this divergence decreases and converges to a finite value; whether the limiting value is $0$ is the conjectured strengthening.

340109.title: The terminal acyclicity-sequence conjecture for matchings
340109.literal_statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $A,B\subseteq G$ be finite sets with $\#A=\#B$. 340110.title: The acyclic matching conjecture with unit acyclicity sequence
340110.literal_statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $A,B\subseteq G$ be finite subsets with $A\cap(A+B)=\emptyset$. Write $\mathcal{M}(A,B)$ for the set of matchings from $A$ to $B$. 340165.title: Eulerian edge-refinement conjecture for discrete spheres
340165.literal_statement:
Let a **$d$-sphere** be a finite simple graph whose unit spheres are $(d-1)$-spheres and which becomes contractible after deleting a suitable vertex. An **edge refinement** is the operation of inserting a vertex into an edge and connecting it to the common neighbors of the edge's endpoints. A graph is **Eulerian** when the degrees of its relevant simplices are even.

**Eulerian edge-refinement conjecture.** $d$-spheres have edge refinements which are Eulerian.

The statement is proposed as a higher-dimensional extension of the result that every $2$-sphere admits edge refinements making it Eulerian. The source specifically says that the corresponding higher-dimensional bootstrapping remains to be established.

340212.title: Parallel dispersion time bound by sequential dispersion and cover times
340212.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph. Write $t_{par}(G)$ and $t_{seq}(G)$ for the parallel and sequential dispersion times, respectively, and let $t_{cov}(G)$ be the cover time.

**Dispersion-time conjecture.**

$$
t_{par}(G) \leq t_{seq}(G)+t_{cov}(G).
$$

This conjecture would imply that the parallel and sequential dispersion times have the same order up to the contribution of the cover time, and could resolve the preceding comparison problem for some classes of graphs. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

340268.literal_statement: Let $P$ be a simple $d$-polytope, and consider its vertex-edge graph. 340389.literal_statement:
Let $G=\prod_{i=1}^t K[a_i,b_i]$ be a direct product of balanced complete multipartite graphs, where $2\leq b_1\leq\cdots\leq b_t$ and $K[a_i,b_i]$ denotes the complete multipartite graph with $b_i$ parts of size $a_i$. Write $\operatorname{IR}(G)$ for the upper irredundance number and $\alpha(G)$ for the independence number. **Strengthened Defant–Iyer conjecture.** If $2\leq b_1\leq\cdots\leq b_t$, then

$$
\operatorname{IR}(G)=\alpha(G).
$$

The paper presents this as a strengthening suggested by methods of Defant and Iyer. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open here.

340479.title: Recurrence conjecture for the coefficients of $W_d(t)$
340479.literal_statement:
Let $W_d(t)$ be a power series, and write $W_d[t^k]$ for the coefficient of $t^k$ in $W_d(t)$. Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $d\geq 2k$. **Recurrence conjecture.** For fixed $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $d\geq 2k$, one has

$$
W_d[t^{k}] = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \Big((-1)^{i+1} \cdot \binom{k}{i} \cdot W_{d-i}[t^{k}] \Big) + 1.
$$

The statement follows a theorem giving a related recurrence for $T(d+k,d)$; the supplied text gives no resolution status for this conjectural analogue.

340516.title: The hare–tortoise fertility gap conjecture
340516.literal_statement:
Let $w$ be a word of length $m$, and let $\langle w\rangle_{\operatorname{\mathsf{hare}}}$ and $\langle w\rangle_{\operatorname{\mathsf{tortoise}}}$ denote its hare- and tortoise-fertilities. **The hare–tortoise fertility gap conjecture.**

$$
\langle w\rangle_{\operatorname{\mathsf{hare}}}-\langle w\rangle_{\operatorname{\mathsf{tortoise}}}\leq\frac{m-5}{2}.
$$

The preceding theorem gives examples of length $2k+5$ attaining a gap of $k$, and the conjecture asserts that these examples are minimal with respect to length.

340531.title: Rota–Welsh conjecture on the Whitney numbers of matroids
340531.literal_statement:

$$
(W_0(M),\dotsc,W_r(M))
$$

est une suite log-concave et donc unimodale; de plus, pour tout entier $k$ tel que $0\leq k\leq r/2$, on a $W_k(M)\leq W_{r-k}(M)$, et

$$
W_0(M)\leq W_1(M)\leq \dotsb \leq W_{\lfloor r/2\rfloor}(M).

340704.title: Path energy monotonicity conjecture for unicyclic graphs
340704.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a unicyclic graph of order $n$ whose cycle has size $k$. The path energy $PE(G)$ is defined for such graphs. **Path energy conjecture for unicyclic graphs.** $PE(G)$ depends only on the parameters $n$ and $k$. For fixed $n$, $PE(G)$ is a monotonically increasing function of $k$. The surrounding text states that the paper gives results resolving Conjectures 2, 3, and 4 from the cited work; this claim is one of those results and is therefore presented as solved.
